articles.title: Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 Narrows Release Window Following Player Feedback
articles.summary: Bandai Namco announced a narrower release window for the upcoming multiplayer-enabled brawler Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3, although it's not too much more specific. Previously, the publisher had stated that the sequel to 2016 fan-favorite would arrive in 2027.
body: "Today we shared more information about battle customization and PvE missions," producer Masayuki Hirano said. "I wanted to use this opportunity to deliver a message to our fans. Over the past several months, we have continuously revealed new information to all of you and, in return, have received valuable feedback. We are truly grateful for that support. Based on the feedback and survey results we have gathered, we have already held discussions with the development team and announced certain areas where we intend to make improvements in response.

"Dragon Ball Xenoverse is a series that we build together with the players through launch, and throughout its post launch life as well," he continued. "To fully realize our ambitions for both the launch experience and the content we plan to operate and support afterward, the release window is currently set for the latter half of 2027." He concluded by suggesting that the team might stay quiet for a while now, saying, "We may keep you waiting a little longer until our next update, but we are fully committed to making 2027 a great year for Dragon Ball game fans, and we will do everything we can to make that happen."
points: Bandai Namco announced a narrower release window for the upcoming multiplayer-enabled brawler Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3, although it's not too much more specific.
Previously, the publisher had stated that the sequel to 2016 fan-favorite would arrive in 2027.

articles.title: Brandon Sanderson Wants to Know Who Really Wrote the Mr. Beast Book
articles.summary: Brandon Sanderson, author of The Cosmere books, has some thoughts on the new Mr. Beast book. More specifically, he is wondering who the true author actually is. During the latest episode of his podcast, Intentionally Blank, he decided to dive into his own perception of The Most Dangerous Games.
body: "I'm really curious who the ghost writer was," said Sanderson. "I would love for them to be credited, but I can see why they're not." He then goes on to explain how he personally goes about co-authoring books, which he recently did with Blightfall, and how he thinks that differs from being an editor. His final point on the matter was "if you see someone else's name on a book, chances are I came up with the outline and then was the editor on it."

For anyone who has followed Mr. Beast's YouTube career, it seems pretty unlikely that he did any of the writing himself. The fact that James Patterson is also listed on the book would make it seem the famous author is likely the one who did all of the heavy lifting to get this story off the ground. But Sanderson questions just how involved Paterson actually was in this project and if the true author is maybe left uncredited.

"Normally it's James Patterson and somebody," explains Sanderson, "what happens in those situations usually is James Patterson has an idea, they brainstorm and outline together, then the person writes the book and Patterson reads it and offers feedback."
points: Brandon Sanderson, author of The Cosmere books, has some thoughts on the new Mr. Beast book.
More specifically, he is wondering who the true author actually is.

articles.title: Star Wars Battlefront 3 Reportedly In Development By EA’s Top Shooter Studios
articles.summary: Included in the shocking news of EA's restructuring, which includes layoffs and the closure of BioWare, is a mention from the publisher that Apex Legends studio Respawn Entertainment and Battlefield maker DICE are collaborating on a project.
body: Per Variety, which cites "multiple sources," the DICE and Respawn project is Star Wars Battlefront 3. While EA itself did not confirm this, the company's memo about the restructuring says that the studios' title will contribute to EA's goal of delivering a "shooter portfolio that unlocks growth."

EA specifically states that learnings from Battlefield 6's launch and live service will further that goal, while also announcing that Apex Legends will be expanded with new "gameplay modes" and "other new experiences."

As for the purported existence of Star Wars Battlefront 3, the timing coincides with a recent rumor that Lucasfilm Games was seeking a development partner for a new Battlefront, and that DICE and Sony-owned studio Bungie were among the studios being considered.

DICE had made two Star Wars Battlefront games for EA, which were released in 2015 and 2017. Battlefront 2 attracted criticism over loot boxes (remember when that was the hot controversy of the day?), but the game still proved to be massively popular. Last year, Battlefront 2 suddenly had a resurgence in players, with many hoping that it would ignite talks of a third Battlefront.

articles.title: GTA 6's Fast Food Restaurant, Burger Shot, Is Coming to Real Life in the Miami Heat's Arena
articles.summary: One of the most iconic fast food restaurants from the GTA universe is becoming real ahead of GTA 6's release. Rockstar Games' takeover of Miami is continuing to expand with a real-life version of Burger Shot, a famous fast-food restaurant in the GTA franchise.
body: It's unclear if the actual menu will be themed after the in-game restaurant, but it's sort of hard to imagine it will be. In GTA, Burger Shot pokes fun at fast food joints like McDonald's and Burger King for their extremely unhealthy meals. In the game, Burger Shot has menu items like "The Heartstopper," which features seven patties stacked high between a variety of toppings.

It seems more likely that this is all purely decorative, but still, it's a fun touch. Additionally, leaks have indicated that Rockstar is also planning to sell some of the beer brands available in GTA 6 at bars in Miami. It's unclear if they will be available in retail stores or online for fans outside of Florida.

Rockstar Games has other ambitious plans for the Kaseya Center, including an unprecdented regular season game where the Miami Heat will turn into the Vice City heat for one night on November 18. The team will be given new jerseys and play on a GTA 6-themed court.

articles.title: Chris Pratt Reaffirms Star-Lord Will Return in the MCU and Plans Are Being Made Right Now
articles.summary: Chris Pratt has confirmed that Star-Lord's return to the MCU is actively being figured out. The beloved galactic hero has been absent from the MCU since 2023, but his last appearance ended with a promise during the credits: Star-Lord will return.
body: “I have a great relationship with Kevin [Feige] and Lou [D’Esposito], and there have been both ongoing conversations about how we make good on that promise and also hard action taken to make sure that we make good on that promise,” he explained. “So yeah, you’ll see Star-Lord again, which is very exciting, but I’m not at liberty to say when that’s going to be, but he’s not going anywhere.”

Of course, Avengers: Doomsday is right around the corner and has a stacked cast... but Pratt is not among the list of confirmed stars. There are some actors who are heavily rumored to appear, but haven't been officially announced. However, Pratt hasn't really been part of the rumor mill. It's possible that he will be in the film's sequel, Avengers: Secret Wars, but we will likely have to wait until next year to know for sure.

articles.title: EA Cancels New Mass Effect, Pauses New Sims Game, And All The Other Big EA News That Just Happened
articles.summary: When EA was acquired by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, many expected major changes at the gaming company, including layoffs and game cancellations, among other shakeups.
body: EA also teased some of what's to come in the future, including a joint project between Respawn and DICE. Here's a rundown of all the big EA news today.

EA said in a statement that it made the "difficult" choice to lay off staff, and Bloomberg reported that the cuts will impact about 400 people. Affected staffers will be treated with "care and respect," EA said, and some impacted employees may have a chance to get a different job within EA. Alongside the BioWare closure noted below, staff at Ripple Effect (Battlefield), Maxis (The Sims), and Full Circle (Skate) have been impacted, as noted by Vertical Slice.

BioWare, the esteemed Canadian developer founded 30+ years ago, is shutting down. The studio employed fewer than 100 people, Bloomberg reported, and the team was working on the next Mass Effect. That game is now canceled.
"BioWare is a legendary studio that helped define the role-playing genre, and we do not take this decision lightly," EA said.

articles.title: The 10 best alchemy cards in Magic: The Gathering, ranked
articles.summary: Love it or hate it, Alchemy fundamentally expanded Magic ’s mechanical lexicon. It proved a digital platform that could just as easily test ideas physically impossible on cardboard as much as it simulated paper play.
body: The most polarizing experiment in Magic: The Gathering history is drawing to a close. When Wizards of the Coast launched Alchemy on MTG Arena in 2021, it promised a digital-native frontier, a platform where cards could be rebalanced overnight and mechanics like Conjure, Seek, and Perpetual could operate unburdened by tabletop constraints. Now, with Wizards officially setting the format's retirement for early 2027, Arena’ s most ambitious design sandbox is entering its final chapter.

Though the dedicated queue is sunsetting, Alchemy’s digital footprint will endure across formats like Historic, Timeless, and Brawl. To understand this chaotic era of digital card design, let’s take a peek at some of the cards that defined it. From format-warping value engines to brilliant structural fixes, here are the 10 cards that best encapsulate Magic 's Alchemy experiment.

"Conceived as a tribute from one French studio to another, these costumes celebrate the creativity, passion, and unmistakably French touch that continue to make the country's video game industry shine on the global stage," Ubisoft said in a press release. Sandfall Interactive is also headquartered in Montpellier.

The friendly homage is no doubt a tribute to Sandfall Interactive and its award-winning debut game, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. The Expedition 33 outfit features a white shirt with black pinstripes, black pants with black suspenders, a red beret, and a baguette kept inside a red-and-white plaid cloth, making it as Gallic as Groundskeeper Willie's introduction to the beautiful French language. Unlocking the outfit for each character in the hit RPG isn't easy, as players must defeat secret mime mini-bosses around the map.

articles.title: Baldur’s Gate 3 Returns With New Official Sequel Series
articles.summary: Baldur's Gate 3 remains one of gaming's most enduring Dungeons & Dragons role-playing games of all time, thanks to its memorable characters, branching story and deep player choice, and extremely generous support from developer Larian Studios.
body: The Last of Us series co-creator Craig Mazin has partnered with Hasbro Entertainment to create a television series for HBO based on Baldur's Gate 3. The new TV show — on which Mazin serves as co-creator, writer, executive producer, and showrunner — is simply titled Baldur's Gate, and its story will pick up where Baldur's Gate 3 left off.

The show will feature both new characters and familiar faces, though no details have been released on which characters will appear in the show, nor who will play them. Because Baldur's Gate 4 is not officially in development, Mazin will likely have a fair amount of freedom when it comes to the show's story, but former D&D's head of creative Chris Perkins will serve as a consultant on the set to ensure the series stays true to its D&D roots.

Mazin, who is a fan of the game and put "nearly 1,000 hours into the incredible world of Baldur's Gate 3," as he said in a statement to Deadline earlier this year, is nothing short of thrilled to be working on the series.

articles.title: The next Mass Effect would have had 'a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has been able to match', according to BioWare veteran
articles.summary: A developer working on Mass Effect 4 has spoken up about BioWare's plans for the now-canceled RPG. Tony de Waal was cinematic supervisor at the now shuttered studio. He joined the team "29+ years ago", left for a spell shortly after the launch of Mass Effect 2, and then returned in 2021 to work on…
body: "I was one of the lucky ones who stayed with BioWare to start on the next Mass Effect [after The Veilguard], where I believe we were making something special: a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has been able to match," de Waal wrote on LinkedIn.
"We saw what Larian and CD Projekt were bringing to the table with their latest offerings, and started down a path to bring Mass Effect to the next level while remaining true to the Trilogy."

De Waal also described some of the challenges BioWare faced during the development of The Veilguard, which was the studio's second project made using EA and DICE's Frostbite engine. "It was a herculean effort that tested the limits of even my workaholic mindset, and I'm proud of the level of polish we were able to pull off in the Frostbite engine.

"Seriously, you have no idea the craziness going on under the hood of that game to make a variable player character work across 3+ hours of cinematics, and the number of conditions to account for in the scenes towards the end of the game."

Those stories are separate from Clayface (also about a Batman villain) and other DC Universe projects, which include Superman, Lanterns, and more movies and TV series.

Deadline 's report on the in-development series has not yet indicated whether this Poison Ivy show would be connected to the larger DCU or if it would take place in a separate universe. Superhero continuity is confusing, regardless of medium. Just ask DC Studios co-head James Gunn.

Poison Ivy, otherwise known as Dr. Pamela Isley, is a sometimes-villain, sometimes-anti-hero ecoterrorist who can control plant life. Outside of comics, her most famous appearances have been in 1997's oft-derided Batman & Robin, where she was played by Uma Thurman, and in the animated sitcom Harley Quinn, where Lake Bell voiced her.

articles.title: Can you identify the horror game by its horrors?
articles.summary: You'd think someone who still screams at the sight of the Tomb Raider T-Rex wouldn't be so into horror games, but I can't help myself; I love 'em. I'm always down for a good inhuman gurgle or unnatural skitter across the floor. Creature with too many eyeballs? Sign me up.
body: Want to keep testing your knowledge of gaming trivia? We've got loads more PC Gamer quizzes, on everything from healthbars to weird currencies to absurd patch notes.

That enthusiasm for terror is why I have the nervous system of a small woodland creature, but also why I can rattle off a list of favorite ghosts and ghouls like they're important historical figures. It's the perfect special interest for a PC Gamer quiz, so today I'm asking: How many horror games can you identify from a screenshot of one of their resident monstrosities?

You've got 12 minutes to face your fears and name as many games as you can from a glimpse of their ghosts, ghouls, and other unspeakable horrors. Let us know how you did in the comments, and then tell us about some of your favorite nightmare encounters.

articles.title: Holy crap, they're making Serious Sam: The Third Encounter
articles.summary: It took almost 25 years to happen, but Serious Sam: The Third Encounter is finally, actually happening. Croteam and Devolver Digital revealed today that a proper new game in the Serious Sam series is now in the early stages of development.
body: I won't pretend to understand this messy continuity, except that each game is sort of a chapter in the story of Serious Sam, which honestly isn't so much a 'story' as it is an excuse to shoot friggin' huge numbers of guys and make the occasional phone call to an all-conquering intergalactic menace named Mental.

That said, Croteam wants everyone to know that The Third Encounter picks up where The Second Encounter left off, so I hope you were paying attention to how it wrapped up 24 years ago: "Not a side story. A true continuation. This time Sam is going to strike Mental's Horde at its heart, and he’s deadly serious about it."

What matters, though, is that this is seriously Serious Sam: "The only thing standing between you and thousands of enemies is your weapon, and the only thing that matters is who pulls the trigger first." That's what I'm here for, baby.
